decisions.decision: T-3-08 threat-model mitigation amended 2026-07-26: OPENPI_DATA_HOME moved from a Drive-backed path to local Colab disk (/content/openpi_data); the checkpoint no longer survives a runtime restart
decisions.rationale: Live Colab run showed gsutil -m cp -r of pi05_libero's 11.6GB/16-shard composite object to a Google Drive FUSE mount is unreliable ('6 files/objects could not be transferred') — a known-poor target for large multi-file parallel transfers. Also installed crcmod with its compiled C extension per gsutil's own official recommendation for composite-object downloads. Accepted trade-off: re-download from GCS on every fresh runtime, which is fast and reliable, in exchange for losing Drive-based persistence across restarts — acceptable for a one-off smoke test (VLA-04), not a production concern.

Only π0's Task 4 checkpoint (re-run with both fixes applied) stands between here and phase completion. Discovered mid-session: this repo's LIBERO/ is its own nested git repo, entirely gitignored by the main repo, but on case-insensitive macOS a pre-existing (Phase 1) convention has files landing under a lowercase 'libero/' path tracked by the MAIN repo's git (not LIBERO's own git) — this is accepted/pre-existing, not something to 'fix' mid-phase. Also discovered: Colab kernels cache Python module imports across cell re-runs — re-syncing a fixed source file via the unzip cell does NOT reload already-imported modules; a genuine Runtime > Restart session is required, not just re-running cells. This caused one confusing false-repeat-error round-trip during debugging; flagged as advisory for any future Colab debugging in this project. Lesson from 260726-epz: openpi tracks main with no pinned release — its LIBERO config names (pi0_fast_libero/pi0_libero) were deprecated in favor of pi05_libero between plan-time and first live run; re-verify openpi's serve_policy.py/README/config.py directly against source before trusting any previously-researched config name if this project's openpi checkout advances again. Lesson from 260726-gj6: do not route large (multi-GB) gsutil/GCS checkpoint downloads through a Google Drive FUSE mount on Colab — use local Colab disk for the download itself, and only copy to Drive afterward (if at all) for persistence; the Drive-mount-as-download-target pattern from Phase 1's HF-token approach does NOT generalize to large multi-file composite-object downloads.
